questions.question: Explain in your own words why every real flow in the circular flow model has a money flow travelling in the opposite direction, using labour as your example.
questions.expected_answer: Nothing in a market economy is given for free: when a household supplies labour (a real flow to firms), the firm pays wages back (a money flow to households). The physical thing and its payment always travel in opposite directions, which is why the diagram shows paired arrows.

questions.question: Why does the comparison between total leakages and total injections determine whether the economy grows, shrinks or stays in equilibrium?
questions.expected_answer: Leakages remove spending from the flow and injections add spending. If more escapes than enters, firms receive less each round, so production and incomes fall; if injections exceed leakages, spending and production rise; when they are equal the flow keeps its size — equilibrium.

questions.question: Describe how you would check your classification of any transaction as a leakage or an injection. Apply your check to a family buying an imported television.
questions.expected_answer: Ask whether the money leaves the domestic spending stream or enters it. The family's money goes to a foreign producer, so it leaves South Africa's flow — a leakage (import). If foreign money had flowed to a South African firm, it would be an injection (export).
